conviction_note: Mild long lean from proxies: an easy Q3 2025 comparison ($211.2M, -34%, cut by tariff-driven retailer order cancellations), Q2 2026 POS double-digit at the top two accounts, US toy industry +17% in H1, and Disguise holding the 2026 KPop Demon Hunters costume license. Against it: the stock is +18% in 20 sessions to a 52-week high at the average price target, management called H2 front-weighted with no holiday theatrical launches, and there is no sourced revenue consensus. abs_move 8 (median reaction 5.1, last three 2.9/10.6/23.7, thin turnover, ~10.5% implied per Unusual Whales but the baseline chain is unusable). p_up 54 gives +0.64, below the findings sum of +1.2, because the run-up and the unsourced revenue bar both pull p_up toward 50.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of about $2.31-2.34. Sources: Small Cap Consumer Research's Q3 estimate of $2.31 (MarketBeat, 2026-07-29, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/small-cap-consu-expects-reduced-earnings-for-jakks-pacific-2026-07-29/) and the TipRanks consensus of $2.33-2.34 (https://www.tipranks.com/stocks/jakk/earnings). The FY2026 EPS consensus is about $1.53-1.64. No Q3 2026 revenue consensus was found, so it is unsourced and every revenue-dependent finding is capped small. The company gives no numeric guidance.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 469K shares at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, 9.3 days to cover (465K, 9.2 days on 09-15), per curvedtrading.com/stocks/jakk/short-interest (page returned 403 to fetch, figures are snippet_only). Against 11.45M shares outstanding (10-Q cover, 2026-07-31) that is about 4% of shares. This is not crowded, but days to cover is high because turnover is thin (20-day average volume about 116K). The baseline has no usable skew: the chain is unusable (ATM spread 145% of mid, open interest 121, put/call OI 0.7). Unusual Whales shows a ±10.5% expected move as of 2026-10-22 (±14% on 10-06). The rise started with a volume spike on 2026-10-01 (296.6K shares) and +6.5% on 10-02, after the 2026-09-25 US-China agreement listed toys for tariff relief. Spot of about $29 sits at the average analyst target (~$29.07, Fintel).

findings.finding: Q3 has an easy comparison and the company's own demand indicators were improving into it. Q3 2025 net sales were $211.2M, down 34%, which the company blamed on retailers cutting direct-import orders over tariffs; Q4 2025 said those disruptions 'abated'. Q2 2026 net sales were $139.2M (+17%), about 7% above the ~$129.6M estimate. The company said POS at its top two US accounts (Walmart 34.3% and Target 23.5% of Q2 sales) was positive in H1 and double-digit in Q2, and that fall planogram and promo shipments were underway in July. EPS consensus of ~$2.31-2.34 implies ~+28% over the $1.80 prior year; no revenue consensus is sourced, so this is sized small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 revenue beat (~7%) was bought +2.9%. Q1 2026 drew +10.6% and Q4 2025 +23.7%. The Q3 2025 revenue miss ($211.2M vs $223.9M) drew -5.1%. Revenue surprises on this name have moved it in the same direction.
findings.why_not_priced: The +18% run-up suggests some of this is priced. But the EPS consensus of ~$2.31 (+28%) was set in late July, before the 2026-09-25 tariff relief and the Hasbro Q3 print, and was trimmed (Small Cap Consumer cut $2.37 to $2.31). If the market had fully priced a recovery to anywhere near the Q3 2024 level ($321.6M), the stock would sit well above the ~$29 average target.
findings.independence: The Q3 2025 base comes from a different document: the Q3 2025 release (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/JAKK/jakks-pacific-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-xqv90ttj7rbm.html). The Q2 2026 numbers come from the 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1009829/000118518526003108/jakkex10-1.htm). The industry series (Circana H1 +17%) is filed as context under finding 3.

findings.finding: Disguise, JAKKS's costume division and the #1 US costume maker by Circana YTD dollars, holds the 2026 North and Latin America license for KPop Demon Hunters costumes, treat pails and pet costumes (announced 2026-03-17). A 2026-10-07 ranking puts it as the #1 Halloween costume of 2026 (201K monthly Google searches). Halloween costumes ship mainly in Q3. NRF projects 2026 costume spend of $4.4B (vs about $4.3B), so the category is flat-to-up and this license is share-gaining. Net of the rest: toys and consumer products are roughly 70% of sales and must not fall back for this to show.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Costumes were +13% in Q1 2026 and +8% in Q2 2026, but no line-specific reaction has been isolated. Q4 2025 costumes fell 28% inside a -3% total, and the stock rose on that print.
findings.why_not_priced: The license is public, but its size in Q3 costume sales is not: the Q2 call did not quantify it and no preview mentions it. If it were priced, the Q3 estimate would have risen since July instead of being trimmed.
findings.independence: The popularity ranking is a different source: Mental Floss, 2026-10-07 (https://www.mentalfloss.com/holidays/halloween/most-popular-halloween-costumes-2026-ranked). Industry spend is NRF, 2026-09-22 (https://talkbusiness.net/2026/09/nrf-2026-halloween-spending-expected-to-rise-3-82/). Both are proxies for sell-through.

findings.finding: Peer and industry context is mixed to positive. Hasbro's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-20, after JAKKS last spoke) shows Consumer Products revenue +4% and North America CP +5% to $504.9M, with full-year guidance raised. Circana US toy dollar sales were +17% in H1 2026, the best in six years, with licensed products and fandom drivers. Target's Q2 (to early August) had Fun 101 up double digits.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured for peer reads on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Likely partly priced: JAKK rose +2.9% on 10-20, the day of Hasbro's print. Hasbro's +5% NA consumer products is a modest number, so the peer read does not support a large sell-in beat. Sized small as a proxy.
findings.independence: Circana via Retail Dive, 2026-08-20 (https://www.retaildive.com/news/us-toy-industry-best-first-half-performance-six-years/828162/). Target Q2 2026 (https://corporate.target.com/press/release/2026/08/target-corporation-reports-second-quarter-earnings). Mattel does not report until 2026-11-05.

findings.finding: Management's own framing caps Q3 upside. On the Q2 call the CFO said 2026 was 'planned ... a bit more front-weighted than normal given the strength of Super Mario' and that there are 'no new toy introductions in the second half supporting holiday theatrical releases'. Outdoor seasonal is in structural decline (-17% YTD). Anime/VTuber revenue is not expected until fall 2027. The CEO said 2026 may 'potentially exceed' initial plans.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No numeric guidance is ever given. On the Q2 print, the same cautious-H2 language was met with +2.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the company said this in July, and the FY EPS consensus (~$1.53-1.64) is built on it. It lands inside what management already told the market, so it is sized toward 0. The residual risk is a soft holiday commentary on the call against a stock up 18% into it.
findings.independence: Shares a document with finding 1 (the same Q2 call transcript), but reads a different passage. The two are not in conflict: finding 1 is the Q3 comparison base, this is the H2 phasing.

findings.finding: The 2026-09-25 US-China agreement put toys (HTSUS 9503.0000, excluding connected toys) on the US list for more favorable tariff treatment, but rates and effective dates still await a Federal Register notice. JAKKS sources heavily from China, and management already said retail prices are unwinding toward pre-tariff levels and improving velocity. Any commentary on the call about lower 2027 cost or pricing is a margin and guide positive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose +1.5% on heavy volume on 10-01 and +6.5% on 10-02, the first sessions after the agreement became widely reported. That move looks like a reaction to it, which suggests most of it is priced.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced in the early-October move. What is left is the company's own quantification on the call, which the market cannot have yet.
findings.independence: Toy Association filings on tariffs (https://toyassociation.org/PressRoom2/News/2026-News/toy-association-opposes-tariffs-across-trade-investigations-and-addresses-toy-drone-disruptions.aspx). This is a macro-to-company proxy that the company has not confirmed.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print +18.2% over 20 sessions, 0.9% off its 52-week high and +93% off its low. At ~$29 it sits at the average analyst target (~$29.07), with no company news explaining the move beyond the 10-01/10-02 tariff-deal jump and the Hasbro day. The bar for the stock is above the published EPS consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4 2025 print (+23.7%) came off a depressed base. No prior print is recorded coming off a +18% 20-day run to a high.
findings.why_not_priced: This finding is itself what the price holds. It is filed because it raises the bar a beat has to clear. Short interest is about 4% of shares with 9.3 days to cover, so a disappointment would not be cushioned by forced covering. A beat could still squeeze on thin turnover.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline (run_up_20d_pct 18.15, pct_from_52w_high -0.94). Fintel's average target ~$29.07 (https://fintel.io/s/us/jakk).

findings.finding: The balance sheet leaves room for a capital-return surprise. Cash was $60.6M at 6/30/26, there is no revolver debt with $68.7M of availability, and the quarterly dividend is $0.25. A $150M shelf was filed 2026-04-30 and nothing has been sold under the ATM. The 2026-09-11 Form 4 cluster is routine director RSU grants and settlements at $24.44, not open-market buying.
findings.why_not_priced: A buyback or dividend increase is optional and unannounced. The unused ATM and shelf are a neutral-to-small overhang, not a negative, because nothing has been sold and cash is ample.

baseline_tension: The findings lean positive while the +18% run-up to a 52-week high cuts against them. There is no usable skew to agree or disagree with, so the run-up is the main thing the lean has to beat. That is why p_up sits only 4 points above 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar): no revenue consensus is sourced and the EPS bar rests on one or two analysts, so the revenue-dependent finding 1 was capped from +1.5 to +1.0.
Rule 9 (segment net of rest): the KPop Demon Hunters costume finding was cut from +1.0 to +0.8, because the license is public and toys (~70% of sales) must also hold up.
Rule 6 (inside guided): the front-weighted H2 comment was already told to the market in July and sits in the FY consensus, so it moved toward 0, from -1.0 to -0.5.

Rule 5/7 (positioning is the baseline to beat, not a document): the run-up finding was cut from -1.5 to -1.0. It raises the bar but is not a fact about the quarter, and short interest (~4%, DTC 9.3) is not crowded either way.
Tariff-deal finding cut from +0.5 to +0.4: a macro-to-company proxy, and the 10-01/10-02 move suggests most of it is priced.
Rule 1 (reaction history) changed nothing: the last three prints were bought (+2.9, +10.6, +23.7), so beats have not been sold on this name.
